claims.statement: langgraph.json registers five graphs (agent, reviewer, analyzer, chat, scheduler) by import path and mounts the FastAPI app agent.webapp:app as the platform HTTP app that owns webhooks and the dashboard API.

langgraph.json configures a checkpointer TTL policy with the delete strategy, a 60-minute sweep interval, and a default TTL of 43200 minutes, and points the platform at the .env file for environment variables.

SANDBOX_TYPE selects the sandbox backend and defaults to langsmith; create_sandbox resolves it against the SANDBOX_FACTORIES registry (langsmith, daytona, modal, runloop, e2b, local) and raises ValueError listing supported types for an unknown value.

validate_sandbox_startup_config runs from the FastAPI lifespan hook so an invalid sandbox-provider configuration fails at server boot rather than at first sandbox creation, delegating to LangSmithProvider.validate_startup_config for the langsmith provider.

Only the langsmith provider honors the snapshot_id and resource overrides passed to create_sandbox; when snapshot_id is omitted the langsmith provider falls back to DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SNAPSHOT_ID, and other providers ignore these options.

For SANDBOX_TYPE=langsmith the base snapshot defaults to DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SNAPSHOT_ID and per-sandbox resources are tuned with optional env vars whose defaults are 128 GiB FS (DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SNAPSHOT_FS_CAPACITY_BYTES), 4 vCPUs (DEFAULT_SANDBOX_VCPUS), 16 GiB memory (DEFAULT_SANDBOX_MEM_BYTES), 7200s idle TTL (DEFAULT_SANDBOX_IDLE_TTL_SECONDS; 0 disables), and 2592000s delete-after-stop (DEFAULT_SANDBOX_DELETE_AFTER_STOP_SECONDS; 0 disables).

A base snapshot is required for SANDBOX_TYPE=langsmith; the server logs a startup warning when neither DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SNAPSHOT_ID nor a stored admin setting is present, and sandbox creation fails until one is configured.

DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SNAPSHOT_ID is only the deployment default; an admin can override the base snapshot at runtime from the dashboard Sandbox page or PUT /dashboard/api/sandbox-settings, and resolve_base_snapshot_id encodes the precedence admin-setting-then-env so the change rolls out without a redeploy.

get_admin_base_snapshot_id is fail-soft: a LangGraph Store lookup error during sandbox creation is caught and returns None so resolution falls back to DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SNAPSHOT_ID rather than failing the run.

get_sandbox_settings reports the stored admin snapshot, the env snapshot, the resolved effective snapshot, and a base_snapshot_source of admin, env, or unset; the stored base_snapshot_id is opaque provider-scoped free text validated only for a 512-character maximum length.
ENVIRONMENT_SNAPSHOT_PREFIX replaces the openswe prefix in environment snapshot capture names so multiple deployments can share one LangSmith workspace without name collisions.

SANDBOX_LANGSMITH_API_KEY (falling back to LANGSMITH_API_KEY / LANGSMITH_API_KEY_PROD) and SANDBOX_LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT (falling back to LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT) point sandbox create/connect/delete, the GitHub proxy config, and snapshot captures at a different LangSmith workspace than tracing.

The primary model id is read from LLM_MODEL_ID defaulting to DEFAULT_MODEL_ID, and the default output/completion token budget is DEFAULT_LLM_MAX_TOKENS (64000), which is a completion budget rather than the context window.

LLM_FALLBACK_MODEL_ID sets an explicit fallback model, defaulting to a provider-appropriate fallback_model_id_for(model_id) when unset, and a ModelFallbackMiddleware is wired only when the fallback differs from the primary model.

Model calls carry a provider-level per-request timeout defaulting to DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (600s) with DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES (6) retries, applied to the openai, anthropic, baseten, google_genai, and fireworks providers so a stalled connection retries instead of parking a run.

ModelCallTimeoutMiddleware imposes a wall-clock deadline around every model call, defaulting to DEFAULT_MODEL_CALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (900s) and overridable with OPEN_SWE_MODEL_CALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, converting a silent transport hang into a ModelCallTimeoutError so the fallback model or run-complete webhook reports it.
Graph runs set recursion_limit to DEFAULT_RECURSION_LIMIT (9999), and the agent and reviewer additionally cap model calls per run at MODEL_CALL_RECURSION_LIMIT (5000) via ModelCallLimitMiddleware.

LangSmith LLM Gateway routing is off by default (LANGSMITH_GATEWAY_ENABLED=false), with LANGSMITH_GATEWAY_API_KEY (falling back to LANGSMITH_API_KEY_PROD then LANGSMITH_API_KEY), LANGSMITH_GATEWAY_BASE_URL, and LANGSMITH_GATEWAY_OPENAI_USE_RESPONSES (default true) tuning it; a per-workspace admin team-settings toggle overrides the env default when set.

RUN_COMPLETE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is a shared bearer token proving a /webhooks/run-complete call came from Open SWE's own dispatch, and verify_run_complete_token fails closed by rejecting every call when the secret is unset, disabling completion and failure replies until it is configured.

The run-completion webhook handler enqueues deferred session-cost refresh for successful Slack runs and posts idempotent failure replies for terminal error/timeout statuses, deduplicating per run id and falling back to a per-thread flag when a run id is absent.

The GitHub App identity is configured with GITHUB_APP_ID, GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY, and GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID, with inbound webhooks verified by GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET; dashboard login uses a separate direct GitHub OAuth (GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_ID/GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_SECRET) distinct from the LangSmith-brokered agent-runtime OAuth (GITHUB_OAUTH_PROVIDER_ID with X_SERVICE_AUTH_JWT_SECRET).

GitHub access tokens must not be stored as deployment environment variables; git and gh inside a LangSmith sandbox authenticate through the sandbox proxy using tokens minted at runtime from GitHub App installation credentials.

ALLOWED_GITHUB_ORGS and ALLOWED_GITHUB_REPOS filter GitHub/Linear webhooks (accepting a repo if its org is allowlisted or its owner/repo is), gate dashboard login, and add a prompt-level edit guard for Slack/dashboard requests, failing closed on GitHub API errors; when both are empty all repos are allowed.

CONFIGURED_ADMINS is a comma-separated GitHub login/email allowlist that determines admin dashboard access (empty means nobody is an admin), and admin-gated API requests also accept GitHub Actions OIDC allowlisted by ADMIN_OIDC_SUBJECTS (empty disables OIDC) with an optional ADMIN_OIDC_AUDIENCE defaulting to open-swe.

OBSERVABILITY_AUTHORIZED_EMAILS is a comma-separated email allowlist for the read-only team observability tools; is_observability_authorized grants access to configured admins unconditionally and otherwise to emails present in this list.

TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY encrypts stored GitHub tokens and accepts an ordered, most-recent-first list of Fernet keys so writes use the first key while reads try each key in order, enabling rotation without invalidating already-stored tokens.

Corridor MCP is enabled when a token is present in CORRIDOR_API_TOKEN, CORRIDOR_MCP_TOKEN, or CORRIDOR_TOKEN (or embedded in the URL query), reads its URL from CORRIDOR_MCP_URL/CORRIDOR_MCP_SERVER_URL defaulting to https://app.corridor.dev/api/mcp, rejects non-Corridor hosts with a warning, exposes only analyzePlan, and keeps credentials in the server process rather than the sandbox.

Datadog MCP credentials live in encrypted team settings and are attached as DD_API_KEY/DD_APPLICATION_KEY headers on a server-side MCP connection, with DATADOG_MCP_TOOLSETS overriding the default core toolset and the sandbox never holding the credentials.
Notion MCP uses per-user OAuth against https://mcp.notion.com/mcp, and NOTION_MCP_CLIENT_NAME (default Open SWE) names the dynamically registered OAuth client.
Currents integration uses a per-user API key against the Currents API base https://api.currents.dev/v1.
